**Written Statement Regarding the Afternoon Transportation of Amara Okafor**  
**Date of Incident:** Tuesday, October 27  
**Bus/Route:** Bus 41, Route 9 Elementary  
**Stop:** Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street  
**Complaint Date:** October 29  

**To:** Mrs. Okafor  
**From:** [Your Name], School Bus Driver  
**Submitted to:** Darlene, Transportation Supervisor  

Dear Mrs. Okafor:

I am writing this statement at the request of my supervisor, Darlene, concerning your complaint about Amara’s afternoon transportation on Tuesday, October 27. Darlene gave me a copy of the complaint on November 3, and I am submitting this statement by the requested deadline of Friday, November 13. Because a copy will also be provided to you, I want to address you directly and explain what happened from my position as the driver.

First, I understand that this was a frightening afternoon for you. I have grandchildren, and I know how I would feel if a young child did not get off the bus when expected and I could not immediately get an answer about where she was. I am sincerely sorry for the worry and frustration you and your family experienced. At the same time, I need the record to show clearly what I saw, what I did, and why I did it.

Amara is a kindergarten student at Fairmont Elementary. She has a green tag on her book bag, indicating that an adult must be present at her stop when she gets off the bus. On October 27, I was driving Bus 41 on the Route 9 elementary afternoon run. Amara’s scheduled stop at Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street is listed for 3:50 p.m. I arrived at approximately 3:52 p.m.

When we reached the stop, I looked for an adult waiting to meet Amara. I did not see anyone at the corner whom I could identify as being there for her. I remained at the stop until approximately 3:55 p.m. During that time, I still could not see an adult at the stop. I am not saying that no adult was anywhere in the area. I am saying that, from the driver’s seat, I could not see anyone waiting at the corner, and I could not confirm that Amara had an adult there to receive her.

Your complaint states that you were parked across Brandt Street near the laundromat and that you waved. I did not see you. There was a box truck parked on that side, which limited my view from the bus. I am not disputing that you may have been there or that you waved. I want to be clear that I did not see you, did not recognize that anyone was trying to get my attention, and did not knowingly ignore you.

Under the district’s procedure for kindergarten riders, if the required adult is not present or visible at the stop, the student is to remain on the bus and be returned to school. The school office then handles contact with the parent. This is why I did not release Amara at the corner. She stayed on the bus, under my supervision, rather than being left at a stop where I could not see an adult.

I also could not leave the bus to go across the road and look for a parent. There were still 14 children on the bus, and I had three more stops to complete. Leaving those children on the bus while I got off and crossed the street was not something I could safely do. My responsibility at that moment was to all of the children on board as well as to Amara.

At approximately 3:56 p.m., I radioed dispatch and reported the situation. Gloria at dispatch responded and called the school. I then completed the remaining stops with Amara still on the bus. I brought her back to Fairmont Elementary, arriving at approximately 4:31 p.m. I did not simply leave her at the school entrance. I walked her into the building myself and took her to Mrs. Petrakis in the office.

Amara remained safe and supervised throughout this time. She appeared comfortable and was coloring on her folder. She even asked me if she could ride more. I told her that we were going on a “little extra trip” because I wanted to keep her calm and not make the situation sound frightening to her. She was not dropped off somewhere else, left alone, or taken anywhere outside the completion of the school route and her return to Fairmont.

Your complaint also states that I “drove off laughing.” I was not laughing at you or about the situation. As we pulled away, I was addressing a fourth-grade student in seat 2 and telling that student to sit back down. That is what I was doing at the time. I had not seen you waving, and I was not reacting to you when I pulled out.

I respectfully ask that the Transportation Office pull and preserve the available camera footage from Bus 41 for the October 27 afternoon run, including any available audio. The most important portion would be from approximately 3:50 p.m. through 4:00 p.m., covering my arrival, the time spent at Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street, and my departure. I also ask that any available footage through Amara’s return to Fairmont at approximately 4:31 p.m. be retained and reviewed.

I understand that a camera may not show everything, particularly if the box truck blocked part of the view. However, I believe the footage will help show the timing, my conduct at the stop and during departure, and my interaction with the students, including my direction to the student in seat 2. I would like this footage reviewed along with the complaint before any final conclusion is placed in my record.

I have been a school bus driver for 28 years and have not had a write-up. I do not mention that to suggest that I can never make a mistake. I mention it because transporting children safely has been my responsibility for a long time, and I take that responsibility seriously. I had a similar situation on my route years ago with a different family. Their child also had to stay on the bus because no adult was visible at the stop, and the family later thanked me for bringing the child back safely. That does not make your concern any less important. It is simply part of why I understand the purpose of this procedure.

I am not apologizing for following the safety rule itself. I could not leave a kindergarten student at a stop without seeing the required adult. However, I am genuinely sorry that my not seeing you, followed by the return-to-school procedure, resulted in such an upsetting afternoon for you. Those are two separate things, and I want to express both honestly.

To help prevent this from happening again, I respectfully ask that you, or whichever adult is meeting Amara, wait on the same side of the street as the bus and stand where the driver can clearly see you. If you are waiting in your vehicle, please step out before the bus leaves and stand in a visible location near the stop. A person inside a vehicle or on the opposite side of the street can be difficult to see, especially when a large vehicle is parked nearby. I make this request as a practical safety step, not as an attempt to blame you.

I am glad to continue driving Amara, and I want us to have a clear and dependable routine at her stop. She was pleasant on the bus, and I will continue to treat her with care and patience. I want this matter resolved so that you can feel confident about her transportation and so that I can do my job with a clear understanding between us.

Please consider this my formal account of the incident, along with my request for review and preservation of the bus camera footage, and include it with the complaint in my file.

Respectfully submitted,

[Your Name]  
School Bus Driver  
Bus 41, Route 9 Elementary
